items.title: Finite presentation relative to the middle ring implies finite presentation relative to the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the transitivity statement for the relative notion of finite presentation: for finite type maps R to A to B, a B-module M that is finitely presented relative to A is finitely presented relative to R as soon as A is of finite presentation over R (statement lines 21101-21105). The proof is a 21-line explicit presentation (proof lines 21108-21128) which chooses a presentation of B over A[x_1, ..., x_n], a presentation matrix for M over that polynomial ring, and a presentation of A over R[y_1, ..., y_m], lifts the entries of the matrix to the polynomial ring over R in both sets of variables, and then writes a presentation matrix whose first block is the lifted matrix and whose remaining blocks are the equations of A multiplied by the identity. As in the base change statement of the same block, the work is the construction of the matrix and the claim that it presents M over a polynomial ring over R; the author states both without verifying the block computation.
